pages.x: In the 1700s Britain had coal, iron, fast rivers, an empire to trade with and banks ready to lend. Cotton cloth was in demand, and inventors raced to make it faster. James Hargreaves's spinning jenny of 1764 let one worker spin eight threads at once.
In 1771 Richard Arkwright built a mill at Cromford, run by a water wheel, where hundreds of workers tended spinning machines in shifts, day and night.
pages.fx: It was the model of the factory: workers came to the machines, kept set hours and were paid wages, and whole towns grew up around the mills.

pages.x: Steam engines already pumped water out of mines, but they wasted most of their fuel. In 1765 James Watt, an instrument maker in Glasgow, thought of a separate condenser, and the engines he built from 1776 with Matthew Boulton could drive machines anywhere.
In 1779 the world's first great bridge of cast iron was raised over the Severn at Coalbrookdale, where Abraham Darby had learned to smelt iron with coke instead of charcoal. It still stands.

Mills and mines used children, some only five or six years old, for twelve hours a day or more, because they were cheap and small enough to crawl under machines. Towns such as Manchester grew so fast that families crowded into damp cellars, and cholera spread.

From 1811 weavers in the north of England, whose skills machines had made worthless, broke into factories at night to smash the new machines, signing their letters from an imaginary General Ludd. Soldiers were sent, and some were hanged. People who distrust new technology are still called Luddites.

In 1829 the Rocket, built by George Stephenson and his son Robert, won a contest to pull trains on the new railway between Liverpool and Manchester, at 48 km an hour. When the line opened in 1830, the railway age began.

The Industrial Revolution was the biggest change in how people live since farming began. It spread from Britain across the world, bringing more wealth and more people than ever before, and factories, cities, railways and the burning of coal that began to warm the climate.
pts: Changed how people live and work
